chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) made a Jew swear by the Torah which was revealed to Moses (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.اسْتَحْلَفَ: He made swear / He administered an oath

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali use the Torah for oaths?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of *istihlāf* (administering an oath) by Imam Ali (AS), demonstrating the validity of using the Torah for legal testimony among Jews in early Islamic society. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of recognizing the scriptural authority of the People of the Book in specific legal contexts, reflecting the pragmatic governance of the Imamate. The incident serves as a foundational precedent for how Islamic courts handled inter-faith legal disputes during the Rashidun and early Umayyad periods.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> got a Jew to swear by the Torah which had been Revealed unto Musa<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
You must make a Jew to take an oath (if needed) by the Torah which was revealed to Musa ‘Alayhi al-Salam .’”
